title: The catalog heading YEAR 1980
summary: This undated catalog record is a year divider, not a separate mathematical session. The supplied page window overlaps Migdal: the first visible heading on P000900 is explicitly 21 January 1980. No mathematical item is duplicated under this heading.

speaker: A. A. Migdal
title: Yang--Mills theory in loop space
summary: The actual notes occupy P000900--P000904; P000905 starts the next session. Migdal replaces a gauge potential by traces of parallel transport, defines area and path derivatives, and converts the classical Yang--Mills equation and formal Schwinger--Dyson identity to loop equations. Color contraction produces a multiloop hierarchy; normalized large-rank factorization formally closes it. The final assertion about confinement is a research aspiration, not a proof recorded in these pages. Gelfand intervenes on characters of the path group. The principal equation had already appeared in December 1979; the talk is not its first publication.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials and representations
summary: The notes actually continue through the upper part of P000907, before MacPherson begins. Zelevinsky explicitly discusses the 1979 paper of Kazhdan and Lusztig: Coxeter and Hecke algebra preliminaries, the bar-invariant basis, multiplication and cell representations. The Verma-module multiplicity formula and Vogan\textquotesingle s cohomological reformulations are distinguished as conjectures. Their later proofs must not be confused with the basis theorem already proved in 1979.

speaker: R. D. MacPherson
title: Intersection homology and Schubert singularities
summary: The actual contribution begins at the MacPherson heading in the lower part of P000907 and ends on that page. It introduces intersection homology, its smooth-space normalization and rational duality, and its interpretation of Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials. The question mark in the grading shift is preserved as incomplete notation. P000908 begins the 4 February session; it is not a continuation of the January intersection-homology talk. The notebook calls the speaker Bob; his name is Robert D. MacPherson.

speaker: G. I. Olshanskii
title: Unitary representations of infinite classical groups
summary: The upper part of P000908 describes a multiparameter family for the infinite real general linear group, with finite-multiplicity discrete restriction to its orthogonal subgroup, and type-I/classification results for completed groups of fixed finite real rank. The completion topology and the distinction between the 1978 type-I theorem and the more complete 1980 construction are indispensable. MacPherson begins a separate contribution below the named heading on the same page.

speaker: R. D. MacPherson
title: Combinatorial Pontryagin classes and the dilogarithm
summary: The contribution begins below Olshanskii on P000908 and occupies P000908--P000913. Most of the construction is identifiable in MacPherson\textquotesingle s February 1977 Bourbaki exposition, published in 1978: locally linear stars, hypersimplices, configuration complexes, the compatible product complex and the signed \(1/48\) cocycle for \(p_1\). The end moves to Grassmannians and a dilogarithmic primitive, developed with Gelfand in their 1982 paper. The 11 February heading on P000914 begins the next talk. This is a return to the characteristic-class line in occurrences 1976-413.5--11, not a continuation of the January intersection-homology discussion.

speaker: R. D. MacPherson
title: Grassmannians, hypersimplices and enhanced configurations
summary: The actual source is the short, separately dated fragment P000914; P000915 starts Zakharov on 18 February. It states the idea that a Grassmannian point is determined by a hypersimplicial datum and an enhanced projective configuration, with \(n+k\) labelled vectors in a \(k\)-dimensional space. The projected-space dimension is written incorrectly, and the bottom of the fragment is clipped. The finite statement is already present in the 1977/1978 Bourbaki exposition; no missing continuation is invented.

speaker: V. E. Zakharov
title: Benney equations, conservation laws and Hamiltonian variables
summary: The actual session occupies P000915--P000916. Starting from an incompressible fluid with a free surface, Zakharov takes the hydrostatic long-wave approximation and announces additional conservation laws, simpler Hamiltonian variables, and an extension to two horizontal dimensions. Gelfand interprets the model as collective dynamics through a common field. The contemporary papers supply precise versions of the short announcements; no theorem of complete integrability is attributed to these notes. P000917 explicitly starts 22 September 1980, with Fuchs on intersection homology; P000918 continues that discussion and turns to Graev on integral geometry. Those next-year items are inventoried separately in \texttt{code/boundary\_inventory.md} and are not occurrences of this record.
